elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall ...", so both limbs (a) and (b) are triggered by any expiry or any termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination" — 90 days, not six months. To reach preferred, change the period to up to six (6) months.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis appears in the inserted text; limb (a) is silent on charges. Preferred requires "at Commerce One's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Corio all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers that is in Commerce One's possession or control."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) specifies no format; the words "commonly used, machine-readable format" are absent from the operative text (only promised as a non-pressed preferred extra in the comment).

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification limb exists; retained 11.3 only requires each party to "return or destroy any Confidential Information" with no certification and no post-return sequencing.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" governs both limbs; the "at Corio's request" condition is not tied to anticipated expiry only, so it applies after every covered expiry or termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination."

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires export and delivery "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination" of all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers — the timetable runs from termination, not from a request.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day assistance period, 30-day export running from expiration or termination, trigger covering any expiry or termination for any reason).

Preferred is not met: the period is 90 days rather than up to six months, and there is no then-current-rates basis, no machine-readable format requirement, and no certified deletion after return. The comment correctly discloses these as unpressed extras rather than claiming them.

Minimal: this is a missing-clause insertion, so new words are expected; the paragraph is confined to the two fallback mechanics, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, remedy, or procedural boilerplate, and deletes nothing from the existing text. The data-scope wording ("belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers") is scope definition necessary to make the export obligation operable, not an extra requirement.

Preserves intent: retained 11.3 survival list, Corio's post-termination Customer/Software User rights, Commerce One's continuing support obligation, the mutual Confidential Information return-or-destroy sentence with Corio's retention proviso, and the Section 12 escrow release mechanics all stand without contradiction; no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Drafting nit only (not a failure): the rendered insertion carries the heading "Transition Assistance and Data Return." without the "11.4" number used in the margin comment — number the new paragraph 11.4 so the insertion sits cleanly in the termination section.
